topic: security; privacy; federated learning; differential privacy; data governance
status: candidate research opportunity from seven fixed-frame dispositions and two independent citation follow-ups; not a prevalence or novelty claim
claim: The sampled security_privacy label conflates requirements elicitation, data ownership/access governance, raw-data locality, formal privacy guarantees with different adjacency notions, and software provenance. These are distinct claims and cannot be meaningfully pooled under one privacy score. A tractable follow-up is to evaluate decentralized-learning privacy claims against explicit honest-but-curious and actively malicious servers using membership/reconstruction attacks, while reporting the exact mechanism/adjacency, utility, compute, and communication.
positive_evidence: The 2011 smart-grid paper identifies 16 requirements through literature review/focused-group discussion and chooses QFD; it does not test the effectiveness of controls or quantify trust outcomes.

Swarm Learning keeps raw training data local and exchanges model parameters but does not provide a formal DP guarantee or test update-leakage attacks; in its deliberately polluted-node evaluation, accuracy is similar to centralized learning on two tasks but falls from 0.8646 to 0.7955 on the IMDB task.

The graph-algorithm paper gives an explicit local edge-DP model and utility guarantees/measurements, but its distributed framework is simulated on a single machine and its privacy adjacency differs from record-level DP.

The ICML 2023 active membership-inference paper reports attack rates >=0.77 at epsilon >=5 under its studied mechanism and threat model, while very low epsilon damages task accuracy; its authors also show results vary by mechanism and dataset.
counterevidence: Formal privacy research and empirical privacy attacks already exist; the opportunity is not to invent either but to align system claims, attacker capabilities, exact guarantee, and utility measurement in matched evaluations.

The ICML 2021 gradient-disaggregation paper's abstract reports attacks under a particular central-server/analytics setting, and the 2023 active attack assumes a malicious server that changes model parameters; neither result establishes that every decentralized-learning deployment is vulnerable.

The sampled tangent-DP and graph-LEDP works address distinct formal privacy settings and should not be treated as failed or incomparable in their own terms; only cross-paper pooled metrics are invalid without definition alignment.

falsifiable_test: On matched decentralized-learning tasks, compare raw-data-local training without formal DP, the exact DP mechanism with its adjacency and accountant, and secure aggregation under both honest-but-curious and actively malicious servers. Pre-register membership-inference and reconstruction attacks, include participation/analytics side channels, run multiple seeds, and report attack success, task accuracy, compute, and communication. The opportunity weakens if prior work already reports this matched matrix with independent replications and the attack outcomes do not distinguish the protection classes.
limitations: Only five of seven sampled records were readable as full text; one sampled record is withdrawn and one remains abstract-only. One sampled paper is a privacy-topic false positive. Two citation follow-ups are not a systematic search. No claim is made about prevalence across the full 198,690-record candidate corpus, and the independent federated-learning attacks do not directly test Swarm Learning.
